headline: The Agent Platform — chat agents with configurable roles, a tool registry, custom personas, admin and manager screens, and an in-app help assistant — is largely backed by code, with two of ten tickets (agent security controls and the command approval workflow) not confirmed from what was examined.
what_is_there: The code shows a working chat agent that can take on different roles, a central registry of tools that separates read-only actions from ones that write or run commands, user-defined agent personas with custom instructions and saved settings, two admin/management screens for creating and editing agents, a floating in-app help assistant, and email alerts when a guardrail blocks an agent action. There is also plumbing that packages skills as reusable, versioned assets seeded into each user's library, even though that ticket is still marked To Do.
what_is_unclear: Two security-related tickets could not be settled: permission gates, command risk classification and audit logging exist as a written policy document but the supporting code was not among the files examined, and the file named for command execution only handles persona directives rather than any approval workflow. This does not mean the work is missing — the analysis only saw part of the codebase.
suggested_action: Ask the team to point to where permission gates, audit logging and the command approval step actually live, and confirm whether the reusable skills ticket should be moved off To Do given the plumbing already present.
